info.title: Scraping Service
info.description: URL scraping service with multi-provider support (Scrape.do default, Firecrawl) - extracts company information from websites

resolvedUrl.description: The URL the page was actually served from, after redirects. Differs from `url` when the site redirects (e.g. a domain forwarded to another company's site): a caller that attributes the content to `url`'s owner should check it. Null only when the provider did not report it.

rawHtml.description: Raw page HTML. Populated only when options.formats includes "rawHtml"; otherwise null. Request-scoped (not cached).

maxAgeDays.description: How old a stored read of this page may be for the call to reuse it instead of reading the page again, in days (whole number, 0 to 7), counted from when that stored content was read. A stored read no older than this is returned free (`cached: true`, whichever org read it); an older one is ignored and the page is read fresh. 0 = always read fresh (same as skipCache: true). Absent = any stored read still kept, i.e. up to 7 days old. Above 7 is refused (400): we keep page content 7 days, nothing older exists. GET /orgs/page-reads lists what is stored and how old it is.

enrich.description: Run company-info enrichment. Defaults to true when omitted (current behavior). Set false to skip enrichment and fetch the raw body cheaply (raw-fetch mode).

render.description: Force scrape.do JS rendering (render=true&super=true). Use for client-rendered pages whose content is not in the initial HTML.

outcomeKey.description: The outcome this scrape produces, stated by the caller. "company_researched" = reading a prospect's company website: on a fresh scrape the scrape run declares it to runs-service, subject = lead-service's company key (`{subjectService: "lead-service", subjectId: <normalized domain of url>}`), so every message using that research consumes it. Omitted = nothing declared: the scrape cost rolls into the caller's nearest declaring run (e.g. brand setup). A cache hit spends nothing and declares nothing. Declaration never fails or slows the scrape.

source.description: map = Firecrawl site map. homepage-links = the map hit its ~18 s ceiling (big site not yet indexed by Firecrawl), so urls are the links found on the homepage instead.

newLinks.description: Links kept by THIS check (one per new referring domain, verified live).

unitsDeclared.description: backlink_earned Units declared on runId by this check (this check's links + any kept earlier whose Unit was not declared yet).

rejected.description: Candidates not kept now (retried by the brand's next check).

truncated.description: The provider held more rows than one call returns (1000).

costMicroUsd.description: treg spend of this check in micro-USD (treg-micro-usd), actualized on runId.

replayed.description: true = the stored answer of a completed check with the same idempotencyKey (nothing spent).

BacklinkProvider.description: Backlink data provider (a tactic the caller may state; closed list). Absent = dataforseo.

id.description: Kept link id = the subject of its backlink_earned Unit (subjectService scraping-service).

domainRank.description: Referring domain authority, DataForSEO rank scale 0-1000 (null = unknown).

firstSeenAt.description: When the provider first saw this domain link to the brand.

verifiedAt.description: When we fetched the referring page and found the link live.

error.description: Named refusal: brand_required (400), wrong_outcome (400), invalid_competitors (400), Invalid request (400), insufficient_credit (402), brand_not_found (404), check_in_progress (409), brand_has_no_site (422), provider_unavailable / billing_unavailable / key_unavailable / brand_service_unavailable / spend_not_declared / outcome_declaration_failed / service_misconfigured (502).

outcomeKey.description: The outcome the caller makes. Must be "backlink_earned"; anything else = 400 wrong_outcome.

idempotencyKey.description: Caller-stated key (e.g. the day). The same key again answers the completed check again: no second spend, no second Unit.

windowDays.description: How far back "new" reaches on the brand's FIRST check (links whose referring domain first linked within this many days). Later checks reuse that first window start, so they count what appeared since.

sources.description: Domains linking to >= minCompetitors competitors and NOT to the brand, most competitors then highest rank first.

minCompetitors.description: Keep a source only when it links to at least this many of the competitors.

minDomainRank.description: Keep a source only when its rank (DataForSEO 0-1000) is at least this. 0 = no floor.

maxSpamScore.description: Drop a source whose known spam score is above this.

units.description: Newest read first. Empty when the org holds none.

nextBefore.description: Cursor of the next (older) page: pass it as `before`. Null on the last page.

hasMore.description: true = older Units exist beyond this page.

url.description: The URL that was asked for.

domain.description: The site's domain: lowercased, no scheme, www., path or port. Null when the URL names none.

ageDays.description: How long ago the page was read, in days, one decimal.

runId.description: The read's own run in runs-service (child of the caller's run); its cost sits there. Null when the run could not be opened.

provider.description: What read the page: scrape-do or firecrawl.

outcomeKey.description: What the caller said the read was FOR (`outcomeKey` on POST /scrape), e.g. "company_researched". Null = the caller stated nothing (e.g. reading a client's own site).

brandIds.description: Brands the read was made for (empty when none was stated).

markdown.description: The page as markdown. Only with includeContent=true and held.

title.description: The page title (or its og:title). Only with includeContent=true and held.

resolvedUrl.description: The URL the page was served from after redirects. Only with includeContent=true and held.

held.description: true = the page content of THIS read is still stored. false = it is gone (deleted after 7 days, or replaced by a later read of the same page, by any org) or was never stored (raw-fetch reads: enrich:false or rawHtml).

resultId.description: Id of the stored content (GET /scrape/{id} returns it), null when not held.

expiresAt.description: When the stored content is deleted (7 days after it was read), null when not held.

units.description: Newest first. Empty when the org holds none.

hasMore.description: true = older Units exist beyond this page.

post.summary: Check the brand's backlinks: keep new live links, declare one backlink_earned Unit each on the caller's run
post.description: Org route called AS the caller's run: headers x-api-key, x-org-id, x-user-id, x-run-id (the run every hold, actual cost and Unit is written on), x-brand-id (exactly ONE brand: the brand whose site is checked), x-campaign-id optional. Reads the referring domains that first linked to the brand's site since the brand's window start (provider via treg, metered on the caller's run: treg-micro-usd held, authorized, actualized), fetches each candidate referring page to verify the link is live now, keeps every verified link new for the brand (one referring domain = one earned link per org x brand, ever), and declares one backlink_earned Unit per kept link on x-run-id (subjectService scraping-service, subjectId = link id). Measured 2026-11-09: one call $0.024 + $0.000036 per row (~$0.026) when nothing is new, ~$0.05 when new domains exist.

200.description: Check answer (new links kept, or nothing new)

502.description: provider_unavailable | billing_unavailable | key_unavailable | brand_service_unavailable | spend_not_declared | outcome_declaration_failed

get.summary: Provider read of backlink_earned: the brand's kept links (x-brand-id), one Unit each
get.description: Org route called AS the caller's run: headers x-api-key, x-org-id, x-user-id, x-run-id (the run every hold, actual cost and Unit is written on), x-brand-id (exactly ONE brand: the brand whose site is checked), x-campaign-id optional. No spend, no run opened, nothing made: it lists what we already hold. One Unit per kept link (a link from another domain to the brand's site that we fetched and found live; one referring domain = one link per org x brand, ever). Unit subject = {subjectService: "scraping-service", subjectId: <link id>}. When it was made: `verifiedAt`. What made it: `declaredRunId`, the run its Unit was declared on (null with `unitDeclared: false` = kept but not declared yet; the brand's next check declares it). The brand is the x-brand-id header (exactly one), the org is x-org-id: a link of another org or brand is never returned. No kept link = 200 with `links: []` and `count: 0`, never 404. Without query filters the answer is every kept link of the brand, oldest first.

get.summary: Provider read of page_read: the web pages this org already had read, one Unit each
get.description: Called AS the caller's run: headers x-api-key, x-org-id, x-user-id, x-run-id. Lists only what the calling org (x-org-id) holds; another org's Units are never returned. Never spends, never opens a run, never reads a page: it lists what we already hold. Nothing held = 200 with `units: []`, never 404. One Unit = one web page read fresh by POST /scrape for this org (a call answered from a stored read made no new read and has no Unit of its own). What we keep of a read: (1) the record of the read, forever: the URL, when, the run, the brands, the campaign, what it was for; (2) the page itself (markdown, metadata, the URL it was served from after redirects) for 7 days, as ONE stored copy per page shared by every org (a later read of the same page, by any org, replaces it), then deleted. `content.held` says whether this read's copy is still there. POST /scrape reuses a stored copy up to 7 days old instead of reading the page again: free, `cached: true`, whichever org read it. To get a fresher page, call POST /scrape with `maxAgeDays` (the oldest stored copy you accept, 0 to 7; 0 = always read fresh). Records start 2026-04-14.

schema.description: Only reads of these pages. 1 to 50 full URLs (with scheme), comma-separated or the parameter repeated. A read matches when its URL names the same page: same host and same path, ignoring the scheme (http/https), a leading www., the port, the query string, the fragment, one trailing slash and letter case. So https://www.Acme.com/pricing/?utm=x matches a read of http://acme.com/pricing, and does not match acme.com/pricing/eu or blog.acme.com/pricing.

get.summary: Provider read of company_researched: the prospect companies whose site this org already had read, one Unit each
get.description: Called AS the caller's run: headers x-api-key, x-org-id, x-user-id, x-run-id. Lists only what the calling org (x-org-id) holds; another org's Units are never returned. Never spends, never opens a run, never reads a page: it lists what we already hold. Nothing held = 200 with `units: []`, never 404. One Unit = one read of a prospect company's website, made by a POST /scrape whose caller stated `outcomeKey: "company_researched"`. The scrape's own run declared it to runs-service with subject {subjectService: "lead-service", subjectId: <the company's domain>}; `runId` is that run. A POST /scrape answered from a stored read (`cached: true`) makes no Unit: nothing was spent, nothing was declared. The same company can have several Units (one per fresh read). `content.held` says whether the page read is still stored (7 days, see GET /orgs/page-reads, which returns the page itself with includeContent=true). History: sales scrapes since 2026-04-14 are included; 4 scrapes of February 2026 predate our records and are not listed.
